title: Lower split-QKV Muon peak LR 0.01 -> 0.007 (square-root batch rule) on the bs-128 incumbent
description: P02 (Muon) follow-up: on incumbent 066-claude (bs 128), lower only the Muon peak LR from 0.01 to 0.007 (~0.01/sqrt(2), the square-root rule for the halved batch), with per-step weight decay held identical via MUON_WD = WD*LR/MUON_LR and AdamW auxiliary, schedule, batch, init and data unchanged. 0.01 was tuned at bs 256 (034 kept; 035 at 0.005 and 055 at 0.015 lost), and at bs 128 each fixed-size orthogonalized step carries twice the gradient noise over twice as many steps, so a smaller step should keep 066's step-count gain while putting less noise into the handoff weights, raising round-1 expert-iteration accuracy on >=7-line targets.
hypothesis: Muon's update size is fixed by orthogonalization, independent of gradient norm, so 066's batch halving doubled both the number of fixed-size steps and the direction noise per step at unchanged LR. Total movement at 0.007 x ~4,760 steps (~33 LR-steps) stays above the bs-256 optimum's 0.01 x 2,339 (~23), so the step-count benefit that made 066 win on every seed (+13/+23/+33) is retained, while noise injected into the hidden matrices per step falls 30%. 067 (bs 64 at 0.01) had one seed collapse to 179, weak evidence that 0.01 is on the high side as the batch shrinks. Lower-noise hidden matrices should hand RL a sharper cap-6 proof prior, raising round-1 >=7-line sample accuracy that compounds over the four EI rounds. Counter-risks: 0.01 may already be optimal at bs 128 (066 won without retuning; 035's 0.005 at bs 256 lost 14), and a less-moved model could under-train in 300 s or extrapolate less to longer proofs.

arch.change: none versus 066-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout, peak Muon LR 0.007 (was 0.01); continuous AdamW auxiliary unchanged from 066-claude

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.007 * adam_lr / 0.001 (peak 0.007, floor 0.0007)
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.change: MUON_LR 0.01 -> 0.007 (~0.01/sqrt(2), square-root batch scaling for 066's halved batch); the only edit to pretrain.py. MUON_WD = WD*LR/MUON_LR recomputes to 0.0142857 so lr*wd is unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*MUON_WD with MUON_WD = WD*LR/MUON_LR = 0.0142857 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (1e-4 per step at peak), so per-step multiplicative decay of every matrix is identical to 066-claude at every schedule fraction; only the orthogonalized update size shrinks to 0.7x.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

batch.change: none versus 066-claude (128 records per optimizer step)
batch.consequences: unchanged from 066-claude: WARMUP 200 optimizer steps, wall-clock cosine, val_loss in batches of 128 (diagnostic only)

config.init: Exactly 066-claude/051: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. The LR does not consume RNG, so initial weights and data-order/shift streams per seed are identical to 066-claude.
